selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main claim made about the person described in this passage?
questions.answer: He is presented as completely truthful and incapable of lying because of his relation to the divine message he delivers.

questions.question: What does the “decree” in his hand refer to?
questions.answer: It refers to the Qur’an.

questions.question: Who is said to have accepted and affirmed this decree across the centuries?
questions.answer: More than three hundred million people in every century.

questions.question: How many kinds of wonder are mentioned for this decree?
questions.answer: Seven.

questions.question: Besides those seven kinds, what other measure of the Qur’an’s extraordinary nature is mentioned?
questions.answer: It is said to have forty aspects of miraculousness.

questions.question: What two major points are said to have been proven elsewhere with strong evidence?
questions.answer: The Qur’an’s miraculous nature and that it is the speech of the Creator.

questions.question: How is the other treatise described in order to show its importance?
questions.answer: It is described as a famous work and compared to the sun within the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What does the continued affirmation of the decree by hundreds of millions indicate about its reception?
questions.answer: It indicates deep and lasting acceptance among people over time.

questions.question: In this passage, what supports the claim that the messenger does not lie: only his personal character, or also the nature of the book he brings?
questions.answer: Also the nature of the book he brings.

questions.question: Give a brief summary of the argument in this paragraph.
questions.answer: The Qur’an is presented as a divine and miraculous decree affirmed across generations, so the one entrusted to convey it cannot be a liar.

questions.question: In this passage, what object is used as a major proof for the truthfulness of the messenger?
questions.answer: The Qur’an is used as a major proof.

questions.question: How is the source of the Qur’an described?
questions.answer: It is described as coming from the Creator of all beings.

questions.question: What does the phrase about every century imply about the decree’s influence?
questions.answer: It implies that its influence is continuous and not limited to one era.

questions.question: Why would lying by the messenger count as a violation of the decree itself?
questions.answer: Because his role is to faithfully deliver and announce it, so dishonesty would go against the message he carries.

questions.question: Why would such lying also count as betrayal toward the One who issued the decree?
questions.answer: Because the decree belongs to Allah, so falsehood in delivering it would break the trust owed to Him.

questions.question: What is the effect of mentioning both the message and the Sender in the final sentence?
questions.answer: It strengthens the argument by showing that lying would be wrong on both levels.

questions.question: Why does this passage not repeat all those proofs?
questions.answer: Because it points readers to that fuller discussion and keeps this section concise.

questions.question: How does the passage use reference to another book without weakening its own point?
questions.answer: It borrows the weight of detailed proof from that book while making a brief clear conclusion here.

questions.question: According to the traveller, what would lying by the messenger amount to in ethical terms?
questions.answer: It would amount to disloyalty and breach of trust.

questions.question: Write the argument of the passage as a short cause-and-effect statement.
questions.answer: Since he faithfully carries and proclaims a divine, miraculous book accepted across ages, deceit cannot belong to him.

questions.question: What is the central focus of this short section: the law, miracles, community history, or the divine book?
questions.answer: The central focus is the divine book.

questions.question: What name is given to that divine book in the passage?
questions.answer: It is called the Qur’an of Mighty Stature.

questions.question: How many broad ways of wonder are mentioned for the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Seven broad ways are mentioned.

questions.question: What does the passage say has already been done in another work regarding the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Its miraculousness and divine origin have already been explained there with solid proofs.
